title: ADA Promotes David Waldschmidt to Senior Vice President
html:
The American Dental Association (ADA) is pleased to announce the promotion of David Waldschmidt, Ph.D., to Senior Vice President, Testing Services & Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE).

In this new role, Dr. Waldschmidt provides strategic and operational leadership for the ADA’s licensure and admissions examination programs, overseeing development, psychometric standards, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, and business growth for a broad portfolio of high-stakes examinations used in professional licensure and educational admissions.

“We rely on robust dental licensure and admissions testing programs to ensure that practicing dentists are skilled and qualified to provide safe and effective oral health care to their patients,” said Nader Nadershahi, D.D.S., M.B.A., Ed.D., Executive Director of the ADA. “During his time at the ADA, Dr. Waldschmidt has played a key role in expanding our services and examination programs. I am confident this growth will continue under his strategic direction as Senior Vice President.”

Dr. Waldschmidt has nearly 30 years of experience in the professional testing industry, previously serving as the ADA’s Senior Director of Testing Services and the JCNDE. He leads the Association’s U.S. and international licensure and admissions high-stakes examination services, working closely with volunteer contributors within the JCNDE and the ADA Council on Dental Education and Licensure (CDEL). His contributions and collaborative efforts have helped advance assessments in dentistry, dental hygiene, and optometry for the benefit of the public and these health professions.

“Testing has tremendous implications for real people in their daily lives,” said Dr. Waldschmidt. “Boards, educational programs, candidates, and the public count on examinations to be valid, reliable, fair, and accurate. It is an honor and a privilege to work with such an exceptional group of highly qualified volunteers and staff, who work tirelessly to make sure we get things right for the benefit of all. I look forward to continuing and expanding upon these important efforts in this new role.”

Dr. Waldschmidt is a staunch advocate for the use of professionally developed assessments to advance oral health care. On the JCNDE’s Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) alone, Dr. Waldschmidt delivered approximately 100 presentations and stakeholder engagements to national and state regulatory, legislative, educational, and professional audiences, including focused presentations in 24 states. In 2026, he received a Presidential Citation from ADA President (2025–2026) Dr. Richard Rosato for guidance and leadership in shaping the future of the examination process.

Dr. Waldschmidt graduated Phi Beta Kappa and summa cum laude with an Honors B.A. in Psychology from Marquette University. He received his M.A. and Ph.D. in Industrial-Organizational Psychology from Michigan State University and the Illinois Institute of Technology, respectively. He currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Association of Test Publishers, a global assessment community that advocates for the valid, reliable, and fair use of assessments to improve outcomes.

About the American Dental Association

The not-for-profit ADA is the nation’s largest dental association, representing 152,000 dentist members. The premier source of oral health information, the ADA has advocated for the public’s health and promoted the art and science of dentistry since 1859. The ADA’s state-of-the-art research facilities develop and test dental products and materials that have advanced the practice of dentistry and made the patient experience more positive.

The ADA Seal of Acceptance has long been a valuable and respected guide to consumer dental care products. The Journal of the American Dental Association (JADA), published monthly, is the ADA’s flagship publication and the best-read scientific journal in dentistry. For more information about the ADA, visit ADA.org. For more information on oral health, including prevention, care and treatment of dental disease, visit the ADA’s consumer website MouthHealthy.org.
